title: Coefficient description and ideal powers in a completed positive monoid algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for the powers of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be a commutative additive monoid generated by finitely many elements, embedded in a free abelian group $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$, and let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Put $A[P]= igoplus_{p\in P}Az^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m,z^p:p
e0)$ and $B=\varprojlim_n A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $p\in P$, let $
u(p)$ be the largest integer $q$ for which $p=p_1+\cdots+p_q$ with all $p_i\in P\setminus\{0\}$; put $
u(0)=0$. This integer is finite. The natural coefficient map gives an isomorphism of $A$-algebras from $B$ to the ring of all families $(a_p)_{p\in P}\in A^P$, with componentwise addition and convolution multiplication $ (ab)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}a_ub_v$. Every sum in this formula is finite. The image of $az^p$ has coefficient $a$ at $p$ and zero elsewhere. For every integer $n\ge1$, the projection $\pi_n:B	o A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak b^nB$, and a family $(a_p)$ lies in this kernel exactly when $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}$ for every $p\in P$. In particular, as $A$-modules, $B/\mathfrak b^nB\cong igoplus_{
u(p)<n} A/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(p)}$, with only finitely many summands.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the displayed formal monoid models, with no regularity assumption on A. Kernel of projection input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, parts (1)--(2) and the final paragraph.

proof.text: Choose nonzero generators g_1, ..., g_s of P (the list is empty when P={0}). Let alpha=min_i w(g_i)>0 when s>0. Every decomposition of p into q nonzero summands has q*alpha <= w(p), so the set of possible q is finite and nu(p) is attained. For each p choose a generator word; if nu(p)<n, a word of length <n can be chosen because its length is at most nu(p). There are only finitely many generator words of length <n, hence S_n={p:nu(p)<n} is finite. If u+v=p, concatenating decompositions gives nu(u)+nu(v)<=nu(p); the same weight bound shows that only finitely many u,v occur. Thus every convolution coefficient below is a finite sum.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; positive-weight finiteness is the agent-supplied coefficient refinement

proof.text: For a finite sum F=sum_p c_p z^p in A[P], one has F in b^n exactly when c_p belongs to m^{max(n-nu(p),0)} for every p. For the forward implication, expand a product of n generators of b: if k factors are nonzero monomials, its coefficient at p is in m^{n-k}, and k<=nu(p); sums preserve the asserted containment. Conversely, if nu(p)<n choose a decomposition of p of length nu(p) and write c_p as a finite sum of products of n-nu(p) elements of m, while if nu(p)>=n choose n nonzero summands in a decomposition of p. Each resulting term lies in b^n, and the support of F is finite, so summing over p proves the reverse implication. The case p=0 uses nu(0)=0 and gives c_0 in m^n.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; finite monomial filtration calculation

proof.text: Write B=lim_n A[P]/b^n. For x=(x_n)_n in B choose finite representatives F_n in A[P]. If m>=n, compatibility and the finite-level criterion give c_p(F_m)-c_p(F_n) in m^{max(n-nu(p),0)}. Therefore, for each p and k, the residue of c_p(F_n) modulo m^k is constant once n>=k+nu(p). Completeness and separatedness of A supply a unique a_p in A with these residues. This defines a coefficient map B to A^P. Conversely, for a family (a_p), the finite set S_n gives a compatible class in A[P]/b^n by summing the terms p in S_n with coefficients a_p modulo m^{n-nu(p)}; changing lifts changes no class by the finite-level criterion. These constructions are inverse because every coefficient is eventually visible modulo every power of m.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; inverse-limit coefficient construction

proof.text: Addition is coefficientwise. For multiplication, representatives multiply by the finite monoid-algebra convolution; for a fixed p only finitely many decompositions p=u+v occur by Step 1, and the stabilized coefficient is sum_{u+v=p} a_u b_v. This proves that the coefficient map is an A-algebra isomorphism onto A^P with convolution. A monomial az^p has the family with coefficient a at p and zero elsewhere, directly from its representatives.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; coefficientwise ring operations

proof.text: The projection pi_n is surjective because the transition maps A[P]/b^m \to A[P]/b^n are surjective: lift a class at level n successively to a compatible inverse-limit sequence. Its kernel consists of families whose nth component is zero. By Step 3 and the finite-level criterion, this is exactly the coefficient condition a_p in m^{max(n-nu(p),0)}. Inclusion b^nB is immediate from the coefficient condition and convolution. For the reverse inclusion, apply the finite-pattern factorization lemma [lem-trf-finite-pattern-factorization] and spell out its finite partition as follows. Choose generators g_1,...,g_s of P and m_1,...,m_t of m. The set S={p:nu(p)<n} is finite by Step 1. For each p in S choose a nu(p)-term decomposition p=p_1+...+p_nu; expand a_p as a finite sum of products of n-nu(p) of the m_j. Each resulting a_p z^p is a product of n generators of b (the m_j constants and the z^{p_i}), so the whole S-part lies in b^nB. For p with nu(p)>=n, choose n nonzero summands and, in a generator word for each summand, choose one generator g_i; cancellativity in the embedding P subset G gives p=g_{i_1}+...+g_{i_n}+q with q in P. There are only finitely many tuples I=(i_1,...,i_n). Assign each such p to the first eligible tuple in a fixed order, and let c^I be the residual family with coefficient a_{g_{i_1}+...+g_{i_n}+q} on the assigned residual q and zero elsewhere. The high-nu part is the finite sum over I of z^{g_{i_1}}...z^{g_{i_n}}c^I, hence is in b^nB. Thus every family satisfying the coefficient condition lies in b^nB, so ker(pi_n)=b^nB.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, parts (1)--(2) and final paragraph; combined with the VI 1.6 finite monomial filtration

proof.text: For a fixed n, the coefficient condition in Step 5 forces a_p=0 modulo the displayed coefficient quotient whenever nu(p)>=n, and leaves the class of a_p in A/m^{n-nu(p)} when nu(p)<n. Since S_n is finite by Step 1, taking these coefficients gives an A-module isomorphism B/b^nB = direct sum_{nu(p)<n} A/m^{n-nu(p)}. The inverse sends a finite tuple to the corresponding finite family, so the isomorphism is explicit.
